name: QWEN-THINKING-BATTERY-0
note: Machine-readable form of PRE-REG QWEN-THINKING-BATTERY-0; the prose governs on any conflict. Part B of Artin's GO QWEN-CHAT-DEFAULT-AND-THINKING-0 (2026-10-23): the frozen 46-task v2 battery (prompts, expected answers and validators byte-identical to QWEN-INFERENCE-BASELINE-0) scored under two new execution configurations with the pinned template's own thinking control enabled: the same 384-token budget as the no-thinking baseline (the controlled comparison) and a 768-token budget (practical usefulness). One run each, no prompt tuning, no retries, budgets fixed here. A reply whose think block closed is scored on the text after its last </think> by the frozen validators; a reply whose think block never closed has no final answer and fails (the hidden reasoning is never searched). Decision rule: bar 3 FIRE reads as thinking recovering the arithmetic and JSON failures; bar 3 NO-FIRE reads as verbosity without recovery at this budget. AMENDED by AMENDMENT QWEN-THINKING-BATTERY-0-RULES (drafted while the chain was live, before any thinking verdict was read): the two-turn kind requires closure on the scored second turn only; a reopened unclosed block is no final answer; format compliance on the final answer only; reasoning tokens to the last close; a fence of one run on every bar (3 tasks; 2 on the 18-task bar). Bars, budgets, prompts, validators and priors unchanged from docs/preregs/qwen-thinking-battery-0.json.

BASELINE.description: the frozen no-thinking receipt logs/qwen_battery/results_v2.json: enable_thinking False, 384 tokens per turn; 33 passes of 46 on the honest count

THINK384.description: enable_thinking True (the template's own control: its reasoning system message and an open think block), 384 tokens per turn, a fresh replay session per task

THINK768.description: the same with 768 tokens per turn

bars.name: THINK-384
bars.description: at the baseline's own 384-token budget, thinking passes at least as many tasks as the baseline (33 of 46).

bars.name: THINK-768
bars.description: at 768 tokens, thinking passes at least as many tasks as the baseline.

bars.name: ARITH-JSON-RECOVERY
bars.description: at 768 tokens, arithmetic plus JSON pass at least 12 of 18 (the baseline passed 8: the ten failures were multi-operand arithmetic and the JSON aggregates); the question of the GO.

bars.name: NO-REGRESSION-768
bars.description: at 768 tokens, code, instruction, two-turn and termination together pass at least 25 of 28 (the baseline's count).

operands.name: the validators and the thinking mapping

refuted_if: The claim that thinking recovers the arithmetic and JSON failures is REFUTED at this budget if bar 3 reads NO-FIRE (fewer than 12 of 18 at 768 tokens). Bars 1, 2 and 4 are reported either way; a bar 4 NO-FIRE names a regression of the kinds the baseline already passed.
registered_prior: The template's thinking mode prepends a system message asking for careful reasoning at xhigh effort and opens a think block; the baseline's two budget-exhausted arithmetic replies spent 384 tokens on working. Expected: at 384 tokens many think blocks never close (the termination tasks, the JSON tasks and the longer code tasks are the likeliest), so bar 1 is expected NO-FIRE with 15 to 30 passes and a budget-exhaustion rate above a third; at 768 tokens most blocks close and the arithmetic and JSON aggregates are expected to improve (bar 3 near its threshold, 10 to 14 of 18) while the termination and instruction kinds risk regressions through exhausted budgets and longer answers (bar 4 a coin flip); bar 2 is expected near the baseline, 30 to 36. Reasoning tokens are expected to dominate generated tokens in both configurations, and first-token latency to be unchanged (the prompt grows only by the system message). Any thinking reply that closes its block and then answers in the wrong format is a format failure of the final answer, scored as the frozen rules score it.
